{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./resnet56v1_bs128.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --time=01:00:00     -> -t 1h
#   -n 1                -> -n 1
#   --gres=gpu:1        -> -g 1

# NOTE: Slurm -p gpu2 not translated.
# Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the gpu2 partition.

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=8000 not translated.
# Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

# NOTE: Slurm -o resnet50-bs128_%A_%a.log uses %A/%a expansions (jobid/array index) which Flux does not provide portably.
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you generate unique filenames.

JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 1h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  cd /home/steinba/development/deeprace/ || exit 1
  pwd

  module load modenv/both modenv/eb tensorflow/1.3.0-Python-3.5.2 docopt/0.6.2 keras/2.1.4 h5py/2.6.0-intel-2016.03-GCC-5.3-Python-3.5.2-HDF5-1.8.17-serial

  # NOTE: Script uses SLURM_ARRAY_JOB_ID / SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID but no --array was specified.
  # Under Flux these variables will not exist. Performance implication: none; operational implication: output TSV name may be wrong.
  # Best-effort: use Flux job id and task rank.
  ARRAY_JOB_ID=${FLUX_JOB_ID:-0}
  ARRAY_TASK_ID=${FLUX_TASK_RANK:-0}

  flux run -n 1 -g 1 python3 ./deeprace.py train -O batch_size=128 \
    -c "k80:1,fs:nfs" \
    -t "/home/steinba/development/deeprace/scripts/short/resnet56v1-short-bs128-${ARRAY_JOB_ID}_${ARRAY_TASK_ID}.tsv" \
    -e 15 resnet56v1
fi
"
}
